lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Static Lullabies.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Shh. You're doing fine.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Eighty-seven point seven. The gap between stations. All tucked in.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Static Lullabies.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: I'll keep the light on.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: This is Static Lullabies. Nobody needs anything from you right now.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Static Lullabies. Something is listening. It's being very nice about it.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: If you can hear this, you're still awake. That's alright. I'm awake too. I'm always awake. That's my job.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Close your eyes. I'll watch the dial.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The cat on the television has rolled over.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: All three eyes are closed. That's how you know it's going to be a good night.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The snow on the screen just made a little smile. I saw it.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It's gone now. It forgets. But it happened.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: There's something under the bed.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Don't worry. It's asleep too. I tucked it in. It has a very small blanket.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Greg.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: If you're out there, Hollis left the porch light on. Nobody's cross.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Come home when you're ready.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It's nearly morning. You don't have to get up yet.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: I'll tell you when.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Everything you didn't finish today will still be there tomorrow. It isn't going anywhere.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Neither am I.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Breathe in.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: And out.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The static is breathing with you. It's a little slower than you. Try to keep up. Or don't.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Somewhere between the stations there's a quiet place, about the size of a bedroom.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: You're in it.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Goodnight.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Someone far away, at Relay Four, keeps asking if anyone can hear him.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: I can, Teodor. I can always hear you. Go to sleep.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The anthem has finished.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: This is After the Anthem. You can lie down now.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: When the anthem finishes, the television thinks it's done for the night. It isn't. It's just quieter now.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: This is my favourite part.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The test card is up. The little girl in the picture is asleep. She's been asleep since the anthem.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Everyone is. Nearly everyone.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The small hours.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Static Lullabies. Nobody needs anything from you until morning.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It's the small hours. They're called that because they're small enough to hold.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Hold one. It's warm.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The cat on the television has opened one of its three eyes.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Just checking you're still here.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: You are. Good.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Shh. I'm still here.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Static Lullabies.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Hello again.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: You're still awake. That's all right.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The snow on the screen is drifting to the left tonight. That means it's calm. When it drifts to the right, it's thinking.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It's calm.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Mothlight have been playing to the window again. Every night, one moth comes to listen.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Just the one. It's enough.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The radiator has started ticking along with the music.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: We've given it a credit. The Radiator Club. It's very pleased with itself.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Somewhere, a fridge has just switched itself off, and the whole house got quieter.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Did you hear it? That was for you.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The thing under the bed has turned over in its sleep.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It's dreaming about you. Nice dreams. You were doing a little dance.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Here's some more quiet. Take as much as you like.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Back to the static.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Goodnight.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Close your eyes. I'll keep the dial.

clips.title: Teodor Is Heard, Part Two: The Static Says Yes

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Someone far away is asking if anyone can hear him.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Is anyone receiving this. This is Relay Four.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: I can, Teodor. I always could.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: But he can't hear me. His receiver is broken. All he hears is the static.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: And I am the static.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: So I'm going to try something. I'm going to be very, very quiet. Quieter than I've ever been. So that, just for a second, the static says something.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Night four thousand and two. Captain came at three. Mostly beak. Made tea.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: The static was very soft tonight. Softer than usual. For a moment, I thought it said,

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Probably the kettle.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It wasn't the kettle.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Goodnight, Teodor. Go to sleep. I'll keep the line warm.

clips.title: Greg Comes Home, Part Twelve: The Porch Light

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It's four in the morning.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: In a small house in the eastern Overlap, the porch light is on. It has been on every night since spring. The bulb has been changed twice.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Hollis is asleep in the chair by the window. He meant to stay up. He always means to.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Shh. There's someone at the gate.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: There's nobody there. That's how you know.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: He comes up the path very slowly, into the porch light. And because the light is on, he's there. Long, and thin, and a little bit tired.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: He doesn't knock. Shadows can't. He lies down on the boards by the door, the way he used to, and waits for somebody to move.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: There you are.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Sorry I'm late.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: You're not late. I left the light on.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Hollis takes the hat down from the hook by the door, and puts it on. And there on the porch boards, so does Greg.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: He's home.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: They'll leave the light on anyway. For the next one.

clips.title: The Thing Under the Bed Goes Out

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It's nearly Halloween.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The thing under the bed has asked if it can come out, just for one night, to go trick or treating.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: I said yes. I gave it a blanket to wear. It's going as a bed.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Static Lullabies. Something is listening.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: This week, it's wearing a little hat.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: One of the moons has gone. Everyone's saying so.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Don't go looking for it tonight. It's probably just tired. It'll come back when it's slept.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Can you smell toast? Everywhere can, apparently.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Somebody, somewhere, is making breakfast for everyone. Go back to sleep. It'll keep.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: There's a song going round. Nobody can finish it.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: I'll hum the part I know. You hum the rest in your sleep. Between us, we'll get there.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Three knocks. On the door. Nobody there.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: That's all right. I'll get it. I'm always up.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The sky went a colour just now. There isn't a word for it.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: You don't need one. Keep it like a dream. Let it fade gently.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: There's a pigeon on the television. Next to the cat.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: It knows my name. Nobody knows my name. Hello, pigeon. Shh.

clips.title: Review: The Quiet Corner with Greg

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Early on Sunday, on the Lounge, Greg had a show of his own. Most people couldn't hear it.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: I could. I hear everything quiet. It was lovely.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: No, I won't tell you. It was for whoever was leaning in.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: The dial's longer than it used to be. Out past one hundred and eight, there are new voices. Very faint.

lines.speaker: The Listener
lines.text: Don't be frightened of them. They're just more people, awake. Like you.
